text:
mia: noticed a perf bump on prod around 14:20 UTC — token p95 jumped from 120ms to 220ms.
sam: saw that in the token-level charts, p50 unchanged but tail doubled :thinking_face:
mia: I opened a quick grafana panel: runtime.token.latency.{prep,kernel,post}.p50/p95 — kernel spikes most.
oliver: any kernel fallback/selector logs? could be falling back to generic xform kernel on certain seq len
mia: adding logs now. infra-bot: commit d4c2a7 deployed to prod (canary)
sam: querying metrics: 
```
sum(rate(runtime.kernel.selection.count{reason="fallback"}[5m])) by (kernel)
``` 
sam: fallback rate -> 0.8 req/s higher last 10m, mostly for long-seq customers
jena: could be KV cache pressure causing larger decodes -> longer kernels? check runtime.kvcache.hit_rate
mia: kv cache hit_rate dropped from 98% -> 87% around the same time
kai: that would increase average seq per request, and kernel selection might choose larger tile sizes triggering slower codepaths
oliver: can we add token-level breakdowns: queue_wait, kernel_exec, kv_lookup, post_process? need p50/p95 per-step
jena: +1 for per-step timers. also batch size histogram (runtime.batch.size_histogram) overlaid with queue.wait
sam: current scheduler only exposes avg_efficiency. we need scheduler.efficiency = serviced_tokens / (gpu_util * time)
mia: I pushed a small PR to add spans in runtime: `span.tags = {step:"kv_lookup"}` and timers emitted as runtime.token.latency.step
ops-bot: started a debug job: loadgen stress test vs prod-model @ 5rps for 15m
oliver: let's also dump kernel selection decisions for a few requests (seq len, batch size, kernel id)
sam: here's a quick log snippet from the canary:
```
[2026-03-17T14:21:03Z] req=abcd seq=768 batch=1 kernel=matmul_v2 selected_by=seq_len
[2026-03-17T14:21:03Z] req=efgh seq=64 batch=12 kernel=fast_v1 selected_by=batch_size
```
mia: interesting — single-request long seqs using matmul_v2 which is slower on our current cuTRT build
jena: plan: 1) add per-step latency metrics + batch size hist 2) surface kernel.selection.* in grafana 3) alert on kvcache.hit_rate < 90% 4) run perf profile (nvprof/cupti) on flagged kernels
kai: I'll wire up a dashboard prototype: panels for token-latency decomposition, batch-size heatmap, scheduler efficiency, kvcache hit rate
sam: also propose a short-term rollback to kernel patch if spike persists. good to have canary cutoff threshold set
mia: thanks — I'll correlate user IDs for top offenders and attach to the perf report
infra-bot: perf job completed: 12 traces collected, upload -> s3://redwood-perf/1769478200/traces.tar.gz
oliver: nice. once we have profiles, we can decide quantization/kernsel changes or scheduler tuning
mia: keeping this thread updated. tagging @product for potential customer impact: they saw higher latency in chat flows
sam: short term dashboard queries I'll add to the PR:
```
- runtime.token.latency.p95 by step
- runtime.batch.size_histogram{route}
- runtime.kvcache.hit_rate{customer}
- runtime.scheduler.efficiency{pool}
```
jena: sounds good. I'll set an alertbook entry and follow up with runbook updates.
kai: prototype dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/queue-and-kernel
mia: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
